# Visual foundations

## Color roles before palette

Inspect the app's theme before selecting new colors. Preserve a customer's brand; Rivet's blue/indigo default is a starting theme, not a requirement for every application. Assign a role to each color rather than adding arbitrary shades per component.

| Role                       | Rivet CSS tokens / Tailwind utilities                                               | Decision                                                        |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Page                       | `--background`, `--foreground`; `bg-background text-foreground`                     | Quiet canvas and primary reading text                           |
| Grouped content            | `--surface`, `--surface-foreground`; `bg-surface text-surface-foreground`           | Separate a meaningful section from its surroundings             |
| Secondary surfaces         | `--surface-secondary`, `--surface-tertiary`                                         | Subtle hierarchy; not a different tint for every region         |
| Floating content           | `--overlay`, `--overlay-foreground`                                                 | Menus, popovers, dialogs use the overlay pair                   |
| Supporting text            | `--muted`; `text-muted`                                                             | De-emphasize metadata; keep required labels readable            |
| Primary action / selection | `--accent`, `--accent-foreground`                                                   | Draw attention to the current action or selection               |
| Status                     | `--success`, `--warning`, `--danger` and their `-foreground` pairs                  | Communicate meaning with text/icon as well as color             |
| Separation / focus         | `--border`, `--separator`, `--focus`                                                | Delineate groups and keep keyboard focus visible                |
| Fields                     | `--field-background`, `--field-foreground`, `--field-placeholder`, `--field-border` | Preserve legibility in idle, focus, invalid and disabled states |

Use component variants for semantic intent: `Button variant="primary"` for the main action, `secondary` for alternatives, `tertiary`/`ghost` for lower emphasis, `danger`/`danger-soft` for destructive actions. Variant vocabularies differ per component; verify them. Reserve accent for meaningful emphasis; several accent-filled panels compete with the primary action. A white surface hard-coded for light mode will fail in dark mode; use paired semantic tokens.

When customizing a theme, update paired foregrounds and both modes. Changes to `--accent` can also require `--focus` and the derived hover/soft colors. Prefer `themeCss`, `themeVariables`, and the contrast helpers from `@rivetjs/ui/theme` for generated themes; see [implementation](rivet-implementation.md). A computed theme is a candidate, not proof of contrast.

Check actual foreground/background combinations, including hover, selected, focus, invalid and overlay states. Use 4.5:1 for ordinary text, 3:1 for large text (at least 24 CSS px regular or about 18.7 CSS px bold), and 3:1 for essential control boundaries/state indicators. Inspect muted labels on their real surface and transparent colors on the composited background. Color-only status and invisible focus indicators fail even when body text passes. Theme audits cover their listed token pairs; custom elements still need inspection.

## Spacing expresses relationships

Rivet's default style kit uses `--spacing: 0.25rem`. Tailwind spacing utilities multiply that base. Reuse the project's existing scale; if none is established, begin with these **design recommendations**, not new library defaults:

| Relationship                                 | Starting range at a 16px root | Typical utilities      |
| -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| Icon and label, tightly related metadata     | 4–8px                         | `gap-1`, `gap-2`       |
| Label/control/help, controls in a toolbar    | 8–12px                        | `gap-2`, `gap-3`       |
| Repeated rows and ordinary component content | 12–16px                       | `gap-3`, `gap-4`       |
| Section padding and related groups           | 16–24px                       | `p-4`, `p-6`, `gap-6`  |
| Distinct page sections                       | 24–32px                       | `gap-6`, `gap-8`       |
| Page gutters                                 | 16px narrow, 24–32px wide     | `px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8` |

Keep space within a group smaller than space between groups. Align headings, fields, rows, and footer actions to shared edges. Pick compact density for repetitive scanning and comfortable density for reading or touch; shrink gaps before shrinking essential text or hit targets. Change density across a whole region, not individual rows.

Use grid/flex gaps for repeated layout and padding at container boundaries. Avoid stacking wrapper padding, card padding, and child margins into accidental whitespace. Do not change global `--spacing` to fix one page: it changes the kit's component dimensions as well. Use a local layout adjustment.

## Typography establishes hierarchy

Use the app's existing font family and weights. When choosing new typography, select a small set of roles rather than assigning a different size to every element. `Typography.Heading` provides semantic `level`, `Typography.Paragraph` supports `size="base" | "sm" | "xs"`, and `Typography.Code` is for code. Verify the installed props before separating heading semantics from visual size.

| Role                         | Practical starting treatment                  |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Page title                   | 24–32px, semibold, tight heading leading      |
| Section title                | 18–20px, medium/semibold                      |
| Reading text                 | 16px, about 1.5–1.75 line height              |
| Dense rows, controls, labels | 14–16px with readable leading                 |
| Secondary metadata           | 12–14px; retain contrast and zoom readability |

These are starting recommendations. The shipped `Typography` h1–h6 styles use Tailwind `text-4xl` through `text-base`; body styles use `text-base leading-7`, `text-sm leading-6`, and `text-xs leading-5`. Inspect project overrides rather than assuming pixel sizes from utility names.

Use one clear page heading and a logical outline. Increase size/weight for a heading before decorating its container. Keep reading columns around 60–75 characters when practical; dense tables and workspaces need different widths. Use tabular numerals for comparable metrics and amounts. Allow important labels to wrap; truncate only scan-oriented content with a way to inspect the full value. Avoid tiny uppercase gray labels as the main way of identifying fields.

## Surface and density discipline

Use a surface/card to establish a distinct object or section. Related settings rows often need one section with separators, not a card per row. Avoid card-inside-card stacks. Use the theme's `--radius` and `--field-radius` and component defaults; adjust them consistently when the brand calls for it. Prefer boundaries, spacing and typography for hierarchy; reserve elevation for floating content and genuinely elevated controls.

For polish, review the screen in grayscale or with accent usage mentally removed: the task and action hierarchy should remain understandable.
